Each scenario’s chart is the average of its runs. Its temperatures and rain come from the same runs at about 550 points over the UK, compared district by district with the 1991–2020 averages from the Met Office HadUK-Grid climate series. Wind comes from each run’s pressure gradient over the UK (the Jenkinson–Collison gale index), and the weather type from the same method’s objective Lamb classification. The description is written from all of this.

The UK sits where the Atlantic meets Europe, beneath the jet stream, between polar and tropical air. Its weather is decided by which air mass arrives — mild and moist from the Atlantic most of the time, but bitterly cold from the continent or the Arctic, or hot from Iberia, when the pattern allows — and by the lows and highs the jet stream steers. Mountains wring rain out of western air and shelter the east; the surrounding seas soften the cold in winter and cool the coasts in spring and summer.
The UK's main air masses by source region. The track the air takes over sea or land modifies it before it arrives.
